beats.say: Golden Retrievers, born from a single yellow puppy in 1864, now one of the world's most loved breeds.
Sir Dudley Marjoribanks bred him at his Scottish estate Guisachan, aiming for the ultimate retriever.
In 1868, he mated that yellow pup with a Tweed Water Spaniel named Belle.
The Kennel Club officially recognised the breed in 1913, and it spread globally.
A 2024 UK study found their median life expectancy is 13.2 years.
All from that one yellow puppy

facts: The Golden Retriever was bred by Sir Dudley Marjoribanks at his Scottish estate Guisachan in the late nineteenth century.
Nous had been whelped in June 1864 and was the only yellow pup in an otherwise all black-coloured litter.
In 1868, Nous was mated to a Tweed Water Spaniel female named Belle
It was recognised by the Kennel Club in 1913
A 2024 UK study found a median life expectancy of 13.2 years for the breed.
